messages:
Jordan H: handing off - overnight we had a P1 that fired for routing->fallback causing a burst of 503s from the hosted API. paging started at ~00:12 UTC, pager volume peaked at 00:18. quick summary:

Jordan H: what happened
- service: routing-proxy (path: /v1/generate)
- symptom: transient 503 spikes and ~3s p95 token latency when fallback routing hit the dedicated pool that was under memory pressure
- trigger: autoscaler concurrent eviction + a buggy config in the fallback policy (weighting set too high to fallback tier)

IncidentBot: ALERT: P1 routing-proxy 503 spike -> 00:12 UTC\- severity: P1\- pages: 00:12,00:13,00:15\- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-proxy-fallback

Tess L: saw the alerts, joining. did we have any long-lived KV evictions or oom kills on the dedicated nodes?

Samir: checking nodes now. found two workers with repeated oom_kill entries since 23:50 UTC. autoscaler removed a few small pods then added back, but the fallback pool got reassigned less capacity than needed. I scaled the dedicated pool +2 GPUs at 00:22 UTC which dropped error rate by ~70% in 6m.

Priya S: customer impact: 9 paid customers experienced degraded responses (timeouts/503) for ~6-12 minutes depending on routing path. Support ticket queue peaked at 00:30 UTC, CS triaged top 3 customers. no data leak, only availability.

Samir: actions taken (chronological):
1) rolled back fallback weighting change (config commit c72f3) -> 00:16 UTC
2) scaled dedicated pool from 6 -> 8 GPUs -> 00:22 UTC
3) forced restart of two problematic workers -> 00:25 UTC
4) bumped autoscaler min-replicas to 6 to avoid immediate scale-in -> 00:28 UTC

Samir: quick commands used:
```
# scale dedicated pool via infra CLI
redwood infra pool scale --name dedicated-routing --replicas 8

# check node oom logs
kubectl -n inference logs pod/routing-worker-123 -c runtime | grep -i oom
```

Tess L: good catch on the config change. where's the PR? we should block that toggle until we have a canary test.

Jordan H: PR is #4127; author toggled fallback weight to 0.7 in prod by accident. I've added a gate to the runbook: fallback-weight >= 0.5 requires canary pass. also added a checklist item to runbook.

IncidentBot: AUTO: Created incident record INC-2026-0422-RP with timeline and pager logs. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0422-RP

Priya S: current status as of last check (00:46 UTC): routing 503s back to baseline, p95 latency trending to normal. support is following up with affected customers. next steps: postmortem draft, change control for fallback toggles, add autoscaler safety margin.

Jordan H: open items for next shift:
- Primary: Tess L (overnight)
- Secondary: Samir (on call until 07:00 UTC)
- Follow-ups:
  * Tess: validate the Canary job for fallback-weight and run two canary cycles in staging today. runbook path: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-proxy-fallback (section: canary)
  * Samir: add metrics for fallback usage (percentage of requests routed to fallback) to the routing dashboard. link: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/routing-proxy
  * Priya: coordinate customer outreach summary and close top-3 tickets with CS notes.

Tess L: ack. I'll run the canary this morning and leave notes. if the canary fails, rollback is:
```
# rollback config to previous stable commit
git checkout c1a5b9 && apply-config staging && run-canary
```

Samir: also recommending adding an autoscaler safety floor to avoid rapid scale-in during traffic lulls. I'll open an infra PR for min-replicas 4 for routing pool.

OpsBot: Action created: OPS-7892 "increase routing autoscaler safety floor" assigned Samir, due 2026-04-01.

Jordan H: retrospective notes:
- root cause: inadvertent config change + autoscaler being too aggressive during low sustained load -> allowed fallback to take disproportionate traffic when dedicated pool temporarily underprovisioned.
- mitigations applied: rollback + scale + restart + increased min-replicas.
- long-term: canary gating for fallback weight changes, dashboard for fallback share, autoscaler guardrails.

Priya S: customers notified. CS will send follow-up emails with incident summary this morning.

Tess L: handing over, will post a short morning update once canary runs. everyone pls ping in this thread if anything spikes. :coffee:

Jordan H: thanks team, handoff complete.

IncidentBot: NOTE: thread closed by IncidentBot at 00:48 UTC.
